A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CADO study. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the added Appendix F in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original TSP and MIS experiments, decoder and fine-tuning ablations, robustness evaluations and TSPLIB results in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports a direct loss–cost correlation analysis and training trajectories in Figure 1c and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The diffusion MDP, REINFORCE objective, standard and label-centered rewards, Hybrid-FT layer selection and inference procedures remain unchanged. The revised explanations introduce no new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same TSP sizes, SATLIB and Erdős–Rényi MIS benchmarks, TSPLIB evaluations and low-quality TSP training scenario. The added plots concern existing tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the matched tables, including RL-Scratch, DIFUSCO+SFT and the FastT2T configurations. Corrected POMO and LKH citations do not change the evaluated methods.

E3.justification: Training budgets, sample counts, metrics, decoder controls and inference settings remain unchanged in Section 6 and Tables 8–12. Appendix F reports trajectories over training schedules already documented in v1.

E4.justification: Figure 1c adds a direct diagnostic of the relationship between SL loss and decoded solution cost. Appendix F adds training-dynamics analyses across five existing tasks; the previous ablations and robustness tests are retained.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly identifies each new Appendix F curve as using one representative fixed seed, while retaining four-run averaging for existing results. This adds seed-reporting information without documenting increased replication or a new uncertainty estimator.

E6.justification: All sixteen tables retain their numerical entries, and the existing figures retain their results. New findings comprise the SL-loss versus cost relationship with R² = 0.038 in Figure 1c and five decreasing optimization-gap trajectories in Figure 5.

T1.justification: V2 removes Section 3's P != NP argument for unavoidable objective mismatch and explicitly assumes exact polynomial-time cost evaluation in Section 4.1. The numbered equations and Appendix A derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the hard-performance-ceiling and essential-alignment claims to an empirical limitation and demonstrated improvement. The introduction and conclusion drop the claim of providing the first direct evidence, while retaining the CADO, LCR, Hybrid-FT and benchmark-performance contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 8 acknowledges inherited labeling and pretraining costs and dependence on the pretrained model. Section 6.2 now interprets sustained loss–cost divergence as suggesting distinct SL and RL optima, while Sections 2.1 and 4.1 clarify applicability conditions.

D1.justification: Figure 1's caption newly identifies TSP-100 as the setting for the existing diagnostic plots. Hardware, checkpoint provenance, architecture and detailed training and inference specifications otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: Several cited works are removed, including da Costa et al. (2020), Dernedde et al. (2024) and Xu et al. (2019), and the first-direct-evidence positioning is dropped. The principal relationship to SoftDIST and T2T/FastT2T remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted paragraph rewrites and terminology clarifications, adds a short Limitations section and Appendix F, and updates publication metadata and bibliography details. Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands from two to three panels, and Figure 5 adds five learning curves. Existing displays are relocated through reflow, including consolidation of Tables 14–16 onto page 21, and journal headers are added; the visual style remains consistent.

improvement.justification: Removing the NP-hardness-based inevitability argument and narrowing the hard-ceiling claim better align the conclusions with the empirical evidence. Figure 1c adds direct diagnostic support, and Section 8 makes pretraining limitations explicit. Appendix F improves training transparency, although its single-seed curves provide limited evidence of reliability. These are useful, modest gains with the method and benchmark results unchanged.
